Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

moral adjective

good and decent, of a person or an act

also morally good, upright, virtuous, honourable, honest, truthful, honorable, honourably

classical

Cic. Amic. 44: ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus
Cic. Fin. 4.25: nec honestō quicquam honestius (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 329

honestus, honesta, honestum

honourable, upright, morally good

Lewis & Short: “honorable, respectable, creditable, worthy, virtuous, decent, proper”. As a noun, honestum is moral goodness, the philosophers’ word for the right. Its first sense is respected, of good standing.

Other words

  • probus, proba, probum — good, honest, upright

    also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 1.5.23 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 154; Traupman 329

    Of persons, upright and honest; of things and craftsmen, good of their kind, excellent (Lewis & Short).

  • vērāx, vērācis — truthful

    also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 5.2.6: sī eris vērāx, tuā ex rē faciēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 329

    Very rare (Lewis & Short).

  • honestē — honourably

    adverb · also used · classical · Traupman 329

Examples

  • haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur, ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus, amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus

    let this, then, be laid down as the first law of friendship: that we ask of friends only what is right, and do only what is right for their sakeCic. Amic. 44

  • breve enim tempus aetātis satis longum est ad bene honestēque vīvendum

    for a short span of life is long enough to live well and honourablyCic. Sen. 70

  • probum patrem esse oportet, quī gnātum suom esse probiōrem quam ipsus fuerit postulat

    a father who demands that his son be better than he was himself ought to be a good manPlaut. Ps. 1.5.23 (Lewis & Short)

See also moral, morals, wrong.
